title: Structured cloning and copying limitations
learningObjectives: Explain structured cloning and copying limitations and use JavaScript collections and iteration safely.

understand.concept: structuredClone() creates a deep copy of supported structured data and can preserve cycles. It supports many built-in data types but cannot clone functions, DOM nodes, or every host object. JSON serialization is more limited and changes or omits some values.
understand.whyItMatters: Choosing the right copy method avoids losing data or sharing nested references unexpectedly. Transferable objects can move ownership of certain resources rather than copying them.
understand.analogy: A structured clone is a carefully reconstructed copy of supported data, not a universal copier for every JavaScript value.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; collection identity, iteration, and binary storage follow JavaScript specification rules.

explain.narrative: The nested object is independently copied, so changing copy.meta does not change source.meta. Functions and unsupported values cause cloning failure.

examples.explanation: The nested object is independently copied, so changing copy.meta does not change source.meta. Functions and unsupported values cause cloning failure.
examples.expectedOutput: Console output demonstrates the collection, iteration, or copying behaviour.

practise.guidedTask: Compare spread, JSON stringify/parse, and structuredClone on nested data, Date, undefined, and a function. Record limitations.
practise.independentTask: Choose an appropriate collection or iteration technique for a small data task. Test duplicates, ordering, identity, and copying behaviour.
hints: Check whether a method mutates its receiver.
Remember that object equality is based on identity.
Use typed arrays only when binary data semantics are needed.
